question.text: The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) was enacted in 1999 to replace which earlier legislation?

answer.text: Reserve Bank of India Act of 1934

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 211 of the workbook states that FEMA was enacted in 1999 to replace the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) of 1973, with the stated objective of consolidating and amending the law relating to foreign exchange to facilitate external trade and payments and to promote the orderly development of the foreign exchange market in India. The Trap: The RBI Act, Banking Regulation Act and SCRA all govern different parts of the financial system and were not the legislation FEMA replaced; only FERA 1973 was the predecessor foreign-exchange statute. Note: The source-backed point is the replacement of FERA 1973 by FEMA 1999 and FEMA's stated objective as set out on page 211.
